standard_prerequisites: Algebra, Lemma algebra-lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian: the I-adic completion of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian
Algebra, Lemma algebra-lemma-Noetherian-permanence: a polynomial ring over a Noetherian ring is Noetherian
Lemma lemma-topologically-finite-type (delivered, L48111): every object of C-prime is the I-adic completion of a finite type A-algebra
Algebra, Lemma algebra-lemma-completion-tensor: for B in C-prime every finite B-module is IB-adically complete
core_obligations: Let A be Noetherian and I an ideal. (1) Every object of C-prime is Noetherian. (2) If B is in C-prime and J is an ideal, then B/J is in C-prime. (3) For a finite type A-algebra C the I-adic completion C^ is in C-prime. (4) In particular A[x_1,...,x_r]^ is in C-prime.
proof_roadmap: Part (4): A[x_1,...,x_r] is Noetherian by algebra-lemma-Noetherian-permanence, hence its completion is Noetherian by algebra-lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian.
Part (1): by lemma-topologically-finite-type every object of C-prime is such a completion, reducing to part (4).

Part (2): B/J is a finite B-module, so algebra-lemma-completion-tensor makes it IB-adically complete, and it is Noetherian as a quotient of a Noetherian ring; part (3) is part (4) applied to C, noting C is Noetherian by the same permanence lemma.
difficulty_reason: H2: a four-part closure statement discharged by a precise citation chain; each part names its carrying lemma, and the one genuine reduction (part (1) to part (4)) is stated with its mechanism.
